description: Catalog of minimal regression counterexamples: each entry is a tiny Selenium C# fixture whose migration must keep a documented invariant, plus the current honest verdict. status=guarded means the invariant IS enforced by the migration today; status=known-gap means the invariant is NOT yet enforced and the residual must stay visible (review/unsupported), never silently closed.

counterexamples.origin: docs/vnext/correctness-risk-areas.md (LOC-01) — locator rewording must be lossless
counterexamples.title: XPath locator rewording is lossless
counterexamples.property: A By.XPath(...) source locator must be re-expressed in the target exactly (same selector), never dropped or replaced by an empty/guessed locator.
counterexamples.whyItIsADefect: A rewritten-but-different selector silently changes which elements the test controls; this is the classic silent locator regression.

counterexamples.origin: docs/vnext/correctness-risk-areas.md (ASRT-03) — grouped fluent assertions must not be silently dropped
counterexamples.title: Assert.Multiple wrapper is never silently elided into nothing
counterexamples.property: A grouped Assert.Multiple body must survive the migration: the wrapper itself is reviewable(elided to a comment) and every nested assertion is individually accounted for — none silently dropped.
counterexamples.whyItIsADefect: Eliding the whole Assert.Multiple to nothing would make every assertion inside disappear while the test still 'passes' the build.

counterexamples.origin: docs/vnext/correctness-risk-areas.md (WAIT-02/03) — custom waits must not become silent no-ops
counterexamples.title: Custom WaitUntil condition is surfaced for mapping, not dropped
counterexamples.property: A project helper that performs a wait must not vanish: it either maps to a Playwright auto-wait with a concrete condition, or remains an explicit reviewable construct.
counterexamples.whyItIsADefect: A wait that silently disappears changes timing semantics (the test no longer waits for the product state it depends on).

counterexamples.origin: docs/vnext/correctness-risk-areas.md (ACT-02) — Actions API has side effects and is not auto-mapped
counterexamples.title: OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions chain is a reviewable construct, not executable target code
counterexamples.property: An Actions(...).Build()/Perform() chain is preserved as an explicit reviewable construct (comment + TODO), never emitted as a fabricated Playwright action.
counterexamples.whyItIsADefect: Actions chains carry ordering and side effects; inventing an executable equivalent (e.g. a bare Click) would change behavior.

counterexamples.origin: docs/vnext/correctness-risk-areas.md (JS) — raw JavaScript execution is side-effectful
counterexamples.title: IJavaScriptExecutor scripts stay reviewable unless explicitly mapped
counterexamples.property: An ExecuteScript(...) call must not be silently counted as transformed or dropped; without a mapped Playwright.Evaluate it is a reviewable residual.
counterexamples.whyItIsADefect: JavaScript with closure/scope side effects cannot be proven equivalent to any fabricated target call.

counterexamples.origin: docs/vnext/correctness-risk-areas.md (LOC-01) + corpus p31 (stale re-query in a loop)
counterexamples.title: Collection re-query inside a foreach is surfaced, not silently re-fetched
counterexamples.property: The source loop iterates a snapshot; a re-query of the collection inside the loop body is preserved as an explicit reviewable residual (raw statement), so the snapshot-vs-live difference is never hidden.
counterexamples.whyItIsADefect: Playwright locators are live; silently iterating a re-query changes which rows are visited and when DOM is re-read.
